text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE FIRED - GPU_MEMORY_PRESSURE - pool=worker-gpu-2 severity=high
pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PD-78342 created and paging: escalation policy 'eng-oncall'
Evan: acked PD-78342 - taking ownership, oncall here
Maria: thx, Evan. any initial customer impact?
Evan: dashboards show a spike in CUDA OOMs for tasks hitting /v1/generate (reranker and embedder). Latency > 10s for ~15% of requests, some 503s.
Jin: seeing repeated logs on node gpu-2b: "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 2.1GiB" and nvlink errors around same time.
Sam: which workloads are failing? embeddings or chat?
Evan: primarily embeddings (embedder service) + reranker. Hosted API fallback to CPU is kicking in but at much higher latency. Customers on Dedicated pools might see evictions.
Leo: rolling back batching increases? could be auto-batcher creating a huge spike. any batch sizes > 4096?
Maria: looking at recent config: worker-gpu-2 has max_batch_tokens=8192 (deployed last night).
Evan: ok reduce that ASAP. actioning: setting max_batch_tokens=2048 for pool worker-gpu-2 via runtime config API now.
Evan: POST /runtime/config -d '{
  "pool": "worker-gpu-2",
  "max_batch_tokens": 2048
}'
incident-bot: runtime-config-change applied (config-service request id=cfg-92a7)
Jin: also setting REDWOOD_PREFETCH=0 on the embedder pods to reduce prefetch footprint.
Sam: can we cordon and drain the worst node? which node has highest OOMs?
Jin: gpu-2b is the hot one. kube node gpu-2b shows dmesg pattern: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID 23456: N/A: GPC0: Xid 79: GPU page fault (invalid address) 
[ 1234.568000] cuda: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at 0x7f1234567000
[ 1234.569000] process embedder-7f4 crashed with OOM during allocation
```
Evan: draining gpu-2b now: `kubectl drain gpu-2b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
Leo: note: draining will evict some long-running inference pods; prefer to scale down there and move traffic first.
Evan: started graceful scale-down of pool worker-gpu-2: `PATCH /pools/worker-gpu-2/replicas {"delta": -2}`
Maria: enabling fallback routing policy to prefer compatible CPU variants for new requests to reduce pressure: `routing.set_policy(pool=worker-gpu-2, fallback=cpu-embedder, mode=immediate)`
Sam: I'm reloading the kvcache eviction parameters too - lowering max_prefix_cache_bytes from 8GB -> 2GB for these nodes.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-78342 acknowledged by Evan. escalation timer paused.
Jin: after lowering batch + cache, OOMs dropped by ~70% on metrics. CPU fallback increased 503->200 but p50 latency jumped.
Evan: informing support to notify affected customers (embed API). Sam, can you draft a short msg?
Sam: draft: "We're investigating elevated GPU memory errors affecting embeddings/reranking. We've temporarily reduced batching and rerouted to CPU fallbacks to restore availability. Working on full recovery; will update in 30m." ok to send?
Maria: yes, add note about mitigation and expected latency impact.
Evan: sent to #support-private and created incident ticket INC-2026.
Leo: should we escalate to infra for possible GPU driver regression? nvlink/kernel traces look noisy.
Jin: Kernel driver appears to be 520.61; last upgrade was 2 weeks ago. I want to repro on a staging node with same driver, but we can also evacuate this pool and rotate it out of rotation for now.
Evan: plan for next 30m: (1) keep reduced batch and cache caps (2) continue draining gpu-2b and replace with fresh instance (3) run driver stress test on replacement node in parallel (4) keep routing fallback enabled until stable.
Sam: putting a reminder: @pagerduty if PD-78342 requires escalation after 30m, page infra on call.
incident-bot: Reminder set for 30m for PD-78342
Evan: thanks team. handoff to Maria for next 30m monitoring while I finish node replacement.
Maria: acked, monitoring dashboards and logs. will update every 10m or sooner on any regression. :thumbsup:
pagerduty: PD-78342 status: acknowledged (Evan) -> in progress
Evan: leaving a short postmortem stub: root cause suspected: aggressive batch config + kvcache pressure exposing driver/kernel instability under high memory allocation churn.
Jin: saving logs to /var/logs/incidents/PD-78342/gpu-2b-oom.log and uploading to incident ticket.
Sam: thanks. closing temporary alert once OOMs < 1% of baseline for 15m.
Maria: update at +20m: OOMs down to 0.3% baseline, CPU fallback serving ~12% of requests for embeddings, latency p95 ~1200ms.
Evan: great, continuing to monitor.
